documents.title: NVIDIA Kumo Forecast Combines Pretrained Time-Series Representations with Historical Pattern Retrieval and Interpretability
documents.text:
NVIDIA Kumo Forecast Combines Pretrained Time-Series Representations with Historical Pattern Retrieval and Interpretability
NVIDIA Kumo Forecast (formerly known as NV-Tesseract Forecasting) is a multi-variate time-series forecasting model that combines a pretrained Transformer backbone with Domain-Aware Representation and Retrieval (DARR), a context-enhanced forecasting mode that blends direct model predictions with patterns retrieved from historical data. This includes interpretability of the results. Built on the MOMENT-1-large backbone, Kumo Forecast uses an approximately 340-million-parameter base encoder plus a trainable forecasting head.
The library provides a DataFrame-first API, configurable forecast horizons, optional historical context for retrieval, and an interpretability framework that produces horizon-specific explanations without modifying the underlying forecaster.
Kumo-Forecast is available under Apache 2.0 license.
Model code: NVIDIA/Kumo-TS
Model weights: nvidia/Kumo-Forecast
A forecasting system can draw on two different sources of information: representations learned during pretraining and historical observations available for the current application. Kumo-Forecast brings these together through a pretrained forecasting model and an optional retrieval pathway over historical context.
In its direct forecasting path, Kumo-Forecast uses a MOMENT-based Transformer and a trained forecasting head to predict future values. In Domain Aware Representation and Retrieval (DARR) mode, it also retrieves related patterns from historical data using a nearest-neighbor approach and combines that information with the direct forecast.
This creates a distinction between the model’s input window and its retrieval context. The input window supplies recent observations for the forecast; a separate historical DataFrame can supply additional context for pattern retrieval. Developers can adjust how strongly the final prediction relies on each pathway through the library’s configuration options.
Further information on DARR mode can be found in this published paper, Memory-Augmented Forecasting: Scalability and Generalization Across Temporal Domains
Kumo-Forecast combines four main components: a pretrained temporal encoder, a trainable forecasting head, historical-pattern retrieval mechanism and an interpretability framework.
Pretrained Temporal Representations: The model uses the MOMENT-1-large Transformer encoder as its backbone. The architecture keeps encoder and embedder weights frozen while training the forecasting head, separating the pretrained representation model from the task-specific prediction layer.
Direct Forecasting: The forecasting head maps the model’s representations to future values for the requested horizon. For horizons beyond the model’s native capability, there is support for autoregressive extension. This distinguishes a directly generated forecast from a longer forecast that extends predictions recursively.
Domain-Aware Representation and Retrieval: DARR augments direct forecasting with k-nearest-neighbor retrieval from historical context data. This process combines direct forecasts with historical-pattern retrieval, while the SDK accepts the historical context through a separate context_df argument.
Interpretability: Kumo-Forecasting also includes a model-agnostic interpretability framework. When enabled, it produces an explanation bundle containing lag and feature attributions per forecast horizon, semantic-flow diagnostics, trajectory-stability diagnostics, and optional embedding Integrated Gradients.These outputs accompany the forecast rather than requiring a different forecasting architecture.
Further details on interpretability can be found in this paper, NVExplain: Explaining Time Series Forecasting with Latent Trajectory Analysis and Structure-Preserving Surrogates
Data must be numeric, temporal data. Supported input sequence lengths include 256, 512, 1024, and 2048 observations. Inputs consist of a timestamp column and one or more numeric value columns, represented as a pandas DataFrame or a CSV/JSON input. When leveraging DARR mode, the dimensions of the context must be similar to the context of the input.
The Factory Operations (FOX) Blueprint includes Early Access to the Predictive Maintenance module which leverages Kumo Anomaly and Kumo Forecast. It analyzes real-time data to predict future anomalies.

We evaluate the method using faithfulness and stability diagnostics across multiple benchmark datasets. Results show that the semantic-flow variant achieves competitive or superior faithfulness compared to standard post-hoc baselines, while being substantially more computationally efficient. Stability analysis further demonstrates that the explanations are robust and identifies regimes where interpretation should be applied with caution.

documents.text:
Kumo-TS is an open-source time series analysis library covering forecasting and anomaly detection. The forecasting module builds on a pretrained transformer backbone; anomaly detection uses diffusion-based models powered by NVIDIA's proprietary algorithms.
- Kumo-Forecast: DataFrame-first API for multivariate time series forecasting with DARR (context-enhanced) mode, built on a vendored backbone.
- Kumo-Anomaly: Diffusion-based multivariate anomaly detection using novel proprietary algorithms.
Clone the repo and install the desired package. Each package has its own environment and lockfile:
git clone https://github.com/NVIDIA/Kumo-TS.git
cd Kumo-TS/Kumo-Forecast
uv sync --frozen --python 3.12   # or: pip install -e .git clone https://github.com/NVIDIA/Kumo-TS.git
cd Kumo-TS/Kumo-Anomaly
uv sync --frozen --python 3.12   # or: pip install -e .
Run each example from its package directory using uv run python, or activate that package’s .venv. Install the packages in separate environments because both expose a top-level sdk module.
from sdk.forecasting import ForecastingConfig, perform_forecasting
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
df = pd.DataFrame({
    "timestamp": pd.date_range("2023-01-01", periods=600, freq="h"),
    "target": np.sin(np.linspace(0, 4 * np.pi, 600)),
    "feature_a": np.random.randn(600),
})
config = ForecastingConfig(
    seq_len=512,
    forecast_horizon=72,
)
for
...
nfig.yaml",
)darr_config = ForecastingConfig(
    seq_len=512,
    forecast_horizon=72,
    alpha=0.2,   # 20% direct, 80% kNN
    k=64,
    temperature=0.05,
)
darr_result = perform_forecasting(
    df=df,
    config=darr_config,
    context_df=historical_df,  # Historical data for kNN retrieval
)
Forecasting includes a model-agnostic interpretability framework that explains why a forecast looks the way it does — without modifying the underlying model. Pass interpretability=True to write an explanation bundle alongside the forecast: lag and feature attributions per horizon, semantic-flow diagnostics, trajectory stability, and optional embedding Integrated Gradients (JSON, CSVs, and PDF report):
interp_config = ForecastingConfig(
    seq_len=512,
    forecast_horizon=72,
    interpretability=True,
    interpretability_output=None,  # "json", "pdf", or None for both
    interpretability_out_dir="interpretability_output",
)
results = perform_forecasting(df=df, config=interp_config)
# Bundle written under interpretability_output/run_<UTC-timestamp>/
See Kumo-Forecast/README.md for the full interpretability reference and artifact catalogue.
from sdk.anomaly_analysis import perform_anomaly_analysis_with_diffusion
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv("your_timeseries_data.csv")
results = perform_anomaly_analysis_with_diffusion(
    df=df,
    threshold_strategy="scs",  # or "macs"
    nsample=15,
)
# Returns original columns + Anomaly (int64: 0 = normal, 1 = anomaly) + MAE (float)
- Python 3.12+ for the installation commands above (Kumo-Forecast declares Python 3.10+; Kumo-Anomaly requires Python 3.12+)
- PyTorch 2.7+
- pandas, numpy
- Pretrained model weights (auto-downloaded from Kumo-Forecast or Kumo-Anomaly on Hugging Face)
- GPU recommended (CUDA or Apple MPS); falls back to CPU automatically
Exact runtime requirements are declared in each package’s pyproject.toml; uv.lock records resolved versions for reproducible installation. See third-party dependencies for the dependency inventory.
- See Kumo-Forecast/README.md for full API reference and examples
- Run Kumo-Forecast/sdk/quick_example.py for an end-to-end example
- Fine-tune on your own CSV with Kumo-Forecast/examples/finetune_example.py
- See Kumo-Anomaly/README.md for detailed usage and configuration
- Run Kumo-Anomaly/examples/quick_example.py for an end-to-end example with synthetic or custom datasets
- Fine-tune on normal windows from your own CSV with Kumo-Anomaly/examples/finetune_example.py

claims.text: Kumo-Forecast uses a vendored transformer backbone for its forecasting module, while Kumo-Anomaly uses diffusion-based models powered by NVIDIA's proprietary algorithms.
claims.evidence_span: The forecasting module builds on a pretrained transformer backbone; anomaly detection uses diffusion-based models powered by NVIDIA's proprietary algorithms.

claims.text: Kumo-Forecast and Kumo-Anomaly packages must be installed in separate environments because both expose a top-level sdk module.
claims.evidence_span: Install the packages in separate environments because both expose a top-level sdk module.

claims.text: Kumo-Forecast SDK provides the perform_forecasting function that accepts a ForecastingConfig object with parameters such as seq_len, forecast_horizon, alpha, k, and temperature for DARR mode.
claims.evidence_span: from sdk.forecasting import ForecastingConfig, perform_forecasting

claims.text: Kumo-Forecast quick example script located at Kumo-Forecast/sdk/quick_example.py provides an end-to-end usage example for the forecasting module.
claims.evidence_span: Run Kumo-Forecast/sdk/quick_example.py for an end-to-end example

claims.text: Kumo-Anomaly quick example script located at Kumo-Anomaly/examples/quick_example.py provides an end-to-end example with synthetic or custom datasets.
claims.evidence_span: Run Kumo-Anomaly/examples/quick_example.py for an end-to-end example with synthetic or custom datasets

claims.text: Kumo-Forecast finetune_example.py script located at Kumo-Forecast/examples/finetune_example.py enables fine-tuning on custom CSV data.
claims.evidence_span: Fine-tune on your own CSV with Kumo-Forecast/examples/finetune_example.py

claims.text: Kumo-Anomaly finetune_example.py script located at Kumo-Anomaly/examples/finetune_example.py enables fine-tuning on normal windows from custom CSV data.
claims.evidence_span: Fine-tune on normal windows from your own CSV with Kumo-Anomaly/examples/finetune_example.py

claims.text: Kumo-Forecast README.md contains the full API reference and examples for the forecasting module.
claims.evidence_span: See Kumo-Forecast/README.md for full API reference and examples

claims.text: Kumo-Anomaly README.md contains detailed usage and configuration documentation for the anomaly detection module.
claims.evidence_span: See Kumo-Anomaly/README.md for detailed usage and configuration
